outcome: No event in the 26 January 2024 to 11 October 2026 window resolves or moves the question as stated. The claimed resolution is older: Carnahan's Generalized Moonshine IV (arXiv 2012, last revised 2016, no journal version found) proves, for Fricke Monster elements, that centraliser characters on twisted modules are Hauptmoduln and says this resolves Norton's conjecture; Carnahan's 51 constructions (arXiv 2017, Communications in Number Theory and Physics 2018) fills the non-Fricke gap and proves a root-of-unity refinement of the constants. Carnahan's 2018 survey calls both Norton's and Ryba's conjectures unconditionally established, but Wikipedia still lists the question as open, and a February 2026 formal-conjectures issue says only special cases are proven.
problem_asks: The bare statement, 'Does generalized moonshine exist?', names a notion it does not define. I took its content from the Wikipedia section the link goes to (Monstrous moonshine article, 'Generalized moonshine' heading) and from the formal-conjectures issue #2149 that restates it. Unpacked: (a) existence, for every commuting pair (g,h) of elements of the Monster group, of a holomorphic function Z(g,h;τ) on the upper half-plane; (b) Z is invariant under simultaneous conjugation of g and h; (c) Z obeys a modular transformation rule under SL₂(ℤ) for each pair, up to a constant; (d) each Z is either constant or a Hauptmodul for some genus-zero congruence group; (e) the normalisation Z(1,1;τ) = j(τ) − 744, with Z = j − 744 exactly when g = h = 1 (the Conway–Norton monstrous moonshine case, which Wikipedia says Borcherds' theorem covers); (f) the representation data: for each Monster element g, a graded projective representation of its centraliser whose traces produce Z. Not part of the bare question but tracked as a refinement: the ambiguous scalar constants in (b) and (c) are roots of unity (Norton 1987), and specifically 24th roots of unity (Norton 2001), and constant-valued Z is a separate case under (d).

events.what_happened: Borcherds proved the Conway–Norton monstrous moonshine conjecture using the Monster Lie algebra built on the moonshine module V♮ (Inventiones Mathematicae, December 1992, per Crossref record). This is the identity case g = h = 1 of Norton's generalized conjecture.
events.delivers: The identity case only: Z(1,1;τ) = j(τ) − 744, i.e. the McKay–Thompson series of the Monster are Hauptmoduln. Wikipedia's Generalized moonshine section says this theorem covers only the case where g is the identity.
events.remains: Every pair (g,h) with g or h non-identity: the functions for nontrivial commuting pairs, the centraliser representation data for nontrivial g, the constants, and the constant-function case.
events.direction: Confirms the identity case of the conjectured properties. Does not address the generalized (commuting-pair) statement.

events.what_happened: Dong, Li and Mason posted 'Some twisted sectors for the Moonshine Module' (arXiv q-alg/9504014, 21 April 1995). The abstract says they give a uniform existence proof for irreducible g-twisted V♮-modules for Monster elements of types 2A, 2B and 4A. A reference list elsewhere places the paper in Contemporary Mathematics vol. 193 (1996); I did not verify this venue.
events.delivers: Existence of irreducible g-twisted V♮-modules for g of types 2A, 2B and 4A. This is the twisted-module input to the centraliser representations in the conjecture, for three classes only. It does not establish the functions Z.
events.remains: All other Monster classes; the Hauptmodul and constant-function properties; all commuting pairs.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture's representation-theoretic input for three classes. No counterexample.
events.object: Irreducible g-twisted V♮-modules for g of types 2A, 2B, 4A, constructed by a uniform existence argument (constructive in the sense of building the modules from the 2A/2B/4A orbifold structure).

events.what_happened: Ivanov and Tuite, 'Rational Generalised Moonshine from Abelian Orbifoldings of the Moonshine Module' (arXiv math/0106027, v1 5 June 2001; v2 26 February 2002 'improved version'; Nucl. Phys. B635 (2002) 435–472). The abstract says they confirm the generalised moonshine conjectures for all rational modular functions, for Monster centralisers related to the Baby Monster, Fischer, Harada-Norton and Held groups, via abelian orbifolds.
events.revisions: v1 5 Jun 2001; v2 26 Feb 2002 (improved version; journal Nucl. Phys. B635 (2002)).
events.delivers: For the listed centralisers only, and only for commuting pairs generating abelian orbifolds with the orders restricted in the abstract (one element of prime order p in {2,3,5,7}, the other of order pk with k = 1 or prime), the generalised moonshine properties hold for rational modular functions (each constant or a genus-zero Hauptmodul).
events.remains: Commuting pairs outside the stated orbifold families; irrational modular functions (a separate paper, Ivanov–Tuite 2002, which Carnahan's Part IV says was conditional on a uniqueness conjecture and on holomorphic orbifold constructions); all other centralisers.
events.doubts: The abstract's scope is restricted to rational functions from abelian orbifolds with the stated orders. Carnahan's Part IV text (per a page-reading tool) says the companion irrational results were conditional.
events.direction: Confirms the conjectured properties in the cases stated. Partial by construction. No counterexample.
events.object: Abelian orbifolds of the moonshine module by commuting Monster elements, whose orbifold partition functions are the rational modular functions; these are the objects whose genus-zero property is checked.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, 'Generalized Moonshine I: Genus-zero functions' (arXiv 0812.3440, posted December 2008; Algebra & Number Theory 4(6) 2010, per search-result metadata). Proves a characterisation of Hecke-monic functions on moduli spaces attached to finite group torsors over elliptic curves: such functions with algebraic-integer coefficients and a pole at infinity are genus-zero functions for a congruence group, or a degenerate type.
events.delivers: A genus-zero characterisation for a class of functions attached to finite-group data. It is an ingredient for the Hauptmodul clause (d), not an existence result for Z.
events.remains: Existence of the functions Z for any commuting pair; the representation data; the constants; the constant-function case.
events.direction: Supports the genus-zero clause. Not a resolution of existence. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, 'Generalized Moonshine II: Borcherds products' (arXiv 0908.4223, posted August 2009; Duke Mathematical Journal 161(5), 2012, per search-result metadata). Builds Lie algebras from infinite product identities and reduces the generalized moonshine conjecture to a pair of hypotheses about group actions on vertex algebras and Lie algebras.
events.delivers: A reduction of the conjecture to two hypotheses. Per search-result summary it does not prove them. It also identifies the 2A case with Höhn's Lie algebra (not separately verified).
events.remains: Both hypotheses, hence the whole conjecture as far as this paper goes.
events.direction: Reduction only. Neither confirms nor refutes the conjecture on its own.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, 'Generalized Moonshine IV: Monstrous Lie algebras' (arXiv 1208.6254; first posted 30 August 2012; v2 24 August 2015; v3 20 August 2016, marked '34 pages, submitted'). Constructs, for each Monster element g, an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra m_g with a projective action of the centraliser of g. For Fricke elements, the centraliser characters on irreducible twisted V♮-modules are Hauptmoduln. The abstract says 'From these results, we resolve Norton's Generalized Moonshine Conjecture.' The arXiv page shows no journal reference or withdrawal.
events.revisions: v1 30 Aug 2012 (77 KB); v2 24 Aug 2015 (40 KB); v3 20 Aug 2016 (44 KB, 34 pages, 'submitted'). No journal reference found.
events.delivers: For Fricke elements only: the centraliser characters are Hauptmoduln, and (per the author) this resolves Norton's conjecture. The paper states the non-Fricke case is deferred, and it does not state in the abstract whether all commuting pairs are covered. It also says it does not treat the root-of-unity constants.
events.remains: Non-Fricke Monster elements (Borcherds–Kac–Moody property left open here, later addressed in Carnahan's 51 constructions); the ambiguous constants (the paper says the constants are not controlled); the constant-function case; scope over all commuting pairs is not explicit in the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: About 14 years since v1 (Aug 2012); last revised Aug 2016; no journal version found.
events.doubts: (1) No journal version found: Crossref query for the title returned no matching record; Carnahan's own publication list (Tsukuba page) lists no entry for it. (2) The paper's own text (per the page-reading tool) says the Borcherds–Kac–Moody property for non-Fricke elements is not proven in full, and postpones it; the 51 constructions paper says it closed that gap later. (3) The constants: Part IV text, as read, does not control the ambiguous constants; the author's later paper says the 2012 argument only gives nonzero constants. (4) Wikipedia (Monstrous moonshine article, last edited 13 August 2026 per the page) still lists the question as open. (5) A formal-conjectures issue opened 3 February 2026 says 'Only special cases have been proven so far', with no source. (6) No independent verification or referee report on the Fricke argument was found. Later papers cite or summarise it but do not check the Fricke argument.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of the conjectured properties for Fricke elements: the paper claims the Hauptmodul and representation statements hold for those elements. No counterexample is exhibited.
events.object: For each Fricke Monster element g, an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra m_g with a projective centraliser action, constructed from an abelian intertwining algebra built from twisted V♮-modules by an 'add a spacetime torus and quantise' construction. The centraliser characters on its irreducible twisted modules are the functions the conjecture asks for, claimed to be Hauptmoduln. The construction is explicit, not an existence-only argument.

events.what_happened: Carnahan and Miyamoto, 'Regularity of fixed-point vertex operator subalgebras' (arXiv 1603.05645, first posted 17 March 2016; v4 13 February 2018, 'additional explanations; 41 pages'). The abstract says it 'resolves one of the principal claims in the Generalized Moonshine conjecture'. No journal reference listed.
events.revisions: v1 17 Mar 2016; v2 4 May 2016; v3 5 Jul 2016; v4 13 Feb 2018 (additional explanations).
events.delivers: If T is a simple, non-negatively graded regular VOA with a nonsingular invariant bilinear form and σ a finite-order automorphism, then the fixed-point subalgebra T^σ is regular; regularity extends to fixed-point subalgebras under any finite solvable group action; and an SL₂(ℤ)-compatibility holds for twisted twining characters of commuting finite-order automorphisms of holomorphic VOAs. Per Carnahan's 2018 survey this supplies claim 4 of the generalized moonshine conjecture (claims numbered there).
events.remains: Per the 2018 survey's own numbering, claims 1, 2 and 5 were earlier and claim 3 is Part IV; the constants and constant-function issues are not addressed by the abstract.
events.time_since_posted: About 7.5 years (v1 Mar 2016); v4 Feb 2018; no journal version found.
events.doubts: Unpublished in a journal as far as found; the abstract does not mention Norton's conjecture by name, so the link to Norton's claim rests on the authors' own phrasing and on Carnahan's 2018 survey.
events.direction: Supports (per authors) one of the principal claims of the conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, 'Fricke Lie algebras and the genus zero property in Moonshine' (arXiv 1701.07846, first posted 26 January 2017; v2 10 July 2017 'final version'). Gives a new proof that canonical actions of finite groups on Fricke-type Monstrous Lie algebras yield genus-zero functions in generalized monstrous moonshine. Carnahan's own publication list gives the venue as J. Phys. A 50(40) (2017); the arXiv page lists DOI 10.1088/1751-8121/aa781d.
events.revisions: v1 26 Jan 2017; v2 10 Jul 2017 ('final version', 19 pages).
events.delivers: The genus-zero property for canonical finite-group actions on Fricke-type Monstrous Lie algebras. The abstract also offers evidence for and against a characterisation of the Monster by these compatibility conditions; it does not claim to prove that characterisation.
events.remains: Existence of the Z functions for all pairs, the constants, the constant-function case, non-Fricke elements.
events.time_since_posted: About 2.5 years before the window; no independent check found.
events.direction: Supports the genus-zero clause for Fricke-type actions. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Johnson-Freyd, 'The Moonshine Anomaly' (arXiv 1707.08388, first posted 26 July 2017; v2 13 September 2017; v3 30 September 2018; Commun. Math. Phys. 365 (2019) 943). The abstract says the moonshine anomaly ω♮ 'has order exactly 24 and is not a Chern class'.
events.revisions: v1 26 Jul 2017; v2 13 Sep 2017; v3 30 Sep 2018; journal Commun. Math. Phys. (2019).
events.delivers: The moonshine anomaly class has order exactly 24. This bears on Norton's proposed refinement that the ambiguous constants are 24th roots of unity, but it does not itself establish existence of the generalized moonshine functions.
events.remains: The existence question entirely; the constant-value refinement depends on the anomaly argument, which Carnahan's 2018 survey says rests on still-conjectural parts of a dictionary between conformal nets and VOAs.

checked_by.who: Communications in Mathematical Physics (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (v3 with the journal reference)

events.doubts: Carnahan's 2018 survey (arXiv 1804.04161) says the proof 'seems to rest on still-conjectural parts of a dictionary relating the theories of conformal nets and vertex operator algebras'. The 51 constructions paper's Section 6 says the 24th-root argument in the 2017 preprint 'does not seem' complete and that the refinement 'rests on still-open conjectures' (both per a page-reading tool; verify verbatim).
events.direction: Concerns the order of the constants, not whether the functions exist. Cuts toward the 24th-root refinement, which the sources describe as conditional.
events.object: The moonshine anomaly class ω♮ in the relevant cohomology of the Monster, of order exactly 24, not a Chern class; proved via a finite-group analogue of T-duality relating it to the Leech lattice CFT anomaly.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, '51 constructions of the Moonshine module' (arXiv 1707.02954, first posted 10 July 2017; v2 18 July 2017; v3 30 March 2021 'final version', 19 pages; Commun. Number Theory Phys. 12(2) (2018) 305–334, DOI 10.4310/CNTP.2018.v12.n2.a3). Abstract: 'prove a refinement of Norton's Generalized Moonshine conjecture'. Uses an orbifold duality with the Leech lattice to show non-Fricke Monstrous Lie algebras are Borcherds–Kac–Moody (Theorem 5.2), closing the gap left in Part IV, and shows the ambiguous constants are roots of unity whenever the function is non-constant.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jul 2017; v2 18 Jul 2017; v3 30 Mar 2021 ('final version'); journal CNTP 12(2) 2018.
events.delivers: (i) Non-Fricke Monstrous Lie algebras are Borcherds–Kac–Moody (Theorem 5.2); (ii) for non-constant functions the ambiguous constants are roots of unity, improving the 2012 claim that they are merely nonzero. Restricted to: non-constant functions; the constant-function case is not controlled; the 24th-root sharpening is not established in this paper (Section 6 says it rests on open conjectures).
events.remains: The constant-function case; the sharper order-24 constants; the Johnson-Freyd dictionary dependence; a remark (Section 7, Remark 7.5, per the page-reading tool) on fixed-point-free automorphisms failing a no-massless-states condition, attributed to unpublished work.

checked_by.who: Communications in Number Theory and Physics (journal of record); referees not named

events.doubts: Section 0.1 of the paper, per the page-reading tool, says 'We will not prove any of these claims about ambiguous constants in their entirety', and Section 6 says the 24th-root refinement is not established. So the peer-reviewed refinement is partial by its own account. The abstract's claim of a refinement of Norton's conjecture is therefore a claim about a restricted form. The Carnahan 2018 survey's 'unconditionally established' is a stronger statement than the 2018 paper's own text.
events.direction: Supports the conjectured structure for non-Fricke elements and the root-of-unity refinement for non-constant functions. Leaves the constant-function case and the 24th-root sharpening open per its own text. No counterexample.
events.object: The non-Fricke Monstrous Lie algebras m_g, which are Borcherds–Kac–Moody Lie algebras, and the identification of certain fixed-point-free automorphisms of the Leech lattice whose cyclic orbifold is isomorphic to the Monster VOA. The orbifold identification is the tool used; it is not itself a counterexample.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, 'Monstrous moonshine over Z?' (arXiv 1804.04161, posted 11 April 2018; RIMS Kōkyūroku 2086 (2018) 91–98 per Carnahan's own list). A survey and speculative paper. Its abstract says both Norton's Generalized Moonshine conjecture and Ryba's Modular Moonshine conjecture have been 'unconditionally established in the last few years'. The body attributes claim 4 to Carnahan–Miyamoto 2016 and claim 3 to Carnahan 2012.
events.delivers: A status claim by the author that Norton's conjecture is unconditionally established (not specified which parts, and by whom beyond the author's own series). The paper also says the Johnson-Freyd 24-root argument rests on a conjectural dictionary, and that there is 'still no control over the constant functions'.
events.remains: By the paper's own account: the constant functions; the dictionary dependence for the 24th-root refinement.

checked_by.who: RIMS Kōkyūroku (conference proceedings; refereeing status not verified)
checked_by.qualification: Proceedings of a research institute symposium

events.doubts: The statement that both conjectures are 'unconditionally established' is the author's own summary of his own series. The arXiv abstract page and the ar5iv rendering give slightly different wordings ('unconditionally resolved' on the abs page; 'unconditionally established' on the ar5iv rendering); verify against the PDF. The same paper says the 24th-root argument depends on conjectural material.
events.direction: Asserts the conjecture is resolved; in the same breath concedes the constant functions and the 24th-root refinement are not controlled. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, 'A Self-Dual Integral Form of the Moonshine Module' (arXiv 1710.00737, first posted 2 October 2017; SIGMA 15 (2019) 030). Constructs a self-dual integral form of V♮ with Monster symmetry; the abstract says this resolves the last open assumption in the Borcherds–Ryba proof of the modular moonshine conjecture (Ryba's conjecture).
events.delivers: Ryba's modular moonshine conjecture (a different problem). The abstract does not mention Norton's generalized moonshine conjecture.
events.direction: Concerns a neighbouring conjecture (Ryba's), not Norton's. Discounted here for scope: it moves a different problem.
events.object: A self-dual integral form of the moonshine VOA with Monster symmetry; it is constructed, and gives a positive-definite self-dual integral form of the 196,884-dimensional Monster representation.

events.what_happened: Carnahan, 'Monstrous Moonshine for integral group rings' (arXiv 2111.09404, posted 2021; IMRN 2024(4) 2748–2789 per CiNii search-result metadata). Proposes a conjecture that Hauptmoduln arise from homomorphisms of representation rings of subgroups applied to an integral form of the moonshine module, and proves it for cyclic subgroups generated by class 4A elements.
events.delivers: A result on integral forms for cyclic subgroups of class 4A. It is a different conjecture (integral group rings), not Norton's generalized moonshine.

checked_by.who: International Mathematics Research Notices (journal of record)

events.direction: A different conjecture. Discounted here for scope.

events.what_happened: Daniel Tan, 'The structure of non-Fricke Monstrous Lie algebras' (arXiv 2507.17854, submitted 23 July 2025). Single author. The abstract gives a structure theorem for Borcherds algebras with no real roots, decomposing them into free, Heisenberg and abelian subalgebras, and identifies a class of these as the Monstrous Lie algebras of non-Fricke Monster elements, with an efficient method for their twisted denominator formulas. The author's comment says 'To appear Contemporary Math (2025)'.
events.delivers: A structure theorem for a class of Borcherds algebras and their identification with a class of non-Fricke Monstrous Lie algebras, plus twisted denominator formulas. The abstract does not claim to resolve Norton's conjecture, and does not say whether it covers all non-Fricke elements.
events.remains: Whether this covers all non-Fricke Monster elements (the abstract says 'a class'); the constants; the constant-function case; the Norton conjecture's commuting-pair scope.
events.time_since_posted: About 15 months at the record date; the 'to appear' publication is not verified.
events.doubts: Only the abstract page was read; the full text was not, so the scope of the identification and any dependence on Carnahan's 51 constructions are not established. The publication 'to appear Contemporary Math' is the author's own comment.
events.direction: Structure and denominator results for a class of non-Fricke Monstrous Lie algebras. Bears on the non-Fricke half of the conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Lisa Carbone, 'Symmetries of Borcherds algebras' (arXiv 2601.10653, submitted 15 January 2026; math.QA, hep-th). The abstract describes it as an overview of the construction of Borcherds algebras, particularly the Monstrous Lie algebras m_g constructed by Carnahan; it discusses their appearance in compactified heterotic-string models, summarises work on Lie group analogues, and includes a discussion of some open problems. The abstract states no new theorems.
events.delivers: No new theorem is stated in the abstract. It is a survey of Monstrous Lie algebras built from Carnahan's results. It does not, in the abstract, state whether Norton's conjecture is established.
events.remains: All of the question, as far as the abstract shows.
events.doubts: The PDF could not be read by the page-reading tool, so its open-problems list and any status statement are unverified. A search-result summary claimed the paper settles the Conway–Norton conjecture 'only in part' for W = V♮; I could not confirm this from the abstract or the readable text.
events.direction: Survey; no claim cutting either way on the existence question from the abstract.

events.what_happened: Lisa Carbone and Elizabeth Jurisich, 'A Magnus group construction for a class of Borcherds algebras' (arXiv 2601.10886, submitted 15 January 2026). Constructs a group for a class of Borcherds algebras and applies it to examples including the Monster Lie algebra and Monstrous Lie algebras of Fricke type.
events.delivers: A group construction (Lie-group analogue) for a class of Borcherds algebras. It does not mention Norton's conjecture and does not address the existence of the generalized moonshine functions.
events.remains: All of the question. Tangential to this problem.
events.direction: No direction on the existence question. Tangential.

events.what_happened: GitHub issue #2149 'Norton's Generalized Moonshine' in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, opened 3 February 2026 by franzhusch. It describes Norton's conjecture (commuting pairs of Monster elements; five properties including the normalisation Z(id,id,τ) = j(τ) − 744), with labels including 'wikipedia' and milestone 'Wikipedia, Group Theory'. Its body states 'Only special cases have been proven so far' without naming a prover. It says 'This issue was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me.' No comments, no linked pull request.
events.revisions: Issue open; no edits visible in the page read.
events.delivers: Nothing mathematical. It restates the conjecture and asserts a status ('only special cases have been proven') that contradicts Carnahan's claimed resolution. It records no new result.
events.remains: All of the question as far as the issue shows.
events.doubts: The status claim 'Only special cases have been proven so far' has no source and names no prover. The issue itself disclaims: 'This description may contain subtle errors especially on more complex problems.' No Lean statement or pull request was found for this problem in the repository search, though the repository tree itself was not browsed.
events.direction: A status assertion that cuts against the claimed resolution. No mathematical direction.

disputes.summary: Conflicting status claims. Carnahan (2012 abstract; 2017 and 2018 papers; 2018 survey 'unconditionally established') and secondary citers (Duncan–Mertens–Ono 2017 and a 2022 'Topological modularity' paper, as summarised in search results) say the conjecture is proven. Against this: Wikipedia's Monstrous moonshine article (labelled 'Unsolved problem in mathematics'; last edited 13 August 2026 per the fetched page) and the List of unsolved problems, which still carries the bare entry with no note; the formal-conjectures issue (3 February 2026) saying 'only special cases have been proven'; and the 51 constructions paper's own text, which says the constant claims are not proven in full and the 24th-root refinement rests on open conjectures.

summary: Found and read: the Carnahan series (Generalized Moonshine I, II, IV; Carnahan–Miyamoto 2016; Fricke 2017; 51 constructions 2017/2018; survey 2018), Johnson-Freyd's moonshine-anomaly paper, the Dong–Li–Mason and Ivanov–Tuite partial-result papers, Borcherds 1992, the 2025–2026 Tan and Carbone papers, the formal-conjectures issue, and the Wikipedia entries. No event in the window resolves or moves the problem as stated. The claimed resolution is Carnahan's Generalized Moonshine IV (arXiv 1208.6254, 2012, last revised 2016): for Fricke Monster elements the centraliser characters on twisted V♮-modules are Hauptmoduln, and the abstract says 'From these results, we resolve Norton's Generalized Moonshine Conjecture.' The non-Fricke case was deferred in Part IV and completed in '51 constructions' (arXiv 1707.02954; peer-reviewed in CNTP 12(2), 2018), which also proves that the ambiguous constants are roots of unity for non-constant functions. Carnahan–Miyamoto 2016 (no journal version found) is cited by the 2018 survey as proving claim 4. The 2018 survey asserts both Norton's and Ryba's conjectures are unconditionally established. I found no journal version of Part IV, no referee report or independent verification of the Fricke argument, and no Monster-specific source describing the constant-function case as settled. Close calls: (a) Part IV's scope over all commuting pairs is not explicit in its abstract; (b) the 51 paper's own Section 0.1 (read through a page-reading tool) says it will not prove the constant claims in full, and Section 6 says the 24th-root refinement is not established; the 2018 survey says the Johnson-Freyd 24-root argument rests on a conjectural dictionary between conformal nets and VOAs. (c) Wikipedia still lists the question as open; the Feb 2026 formal-conjectures issue says only special cases are proven, without a source. The in-window items are Tan 2025 (structure theorem for a class of non-Fricke Monstrous Lie algebras; 'to appear' in Contemporary Math), Carbone 2026 (survey; no new theorem in the abstract), Carbone–Jurisich 2026 (group construction; tangential), and the formal-conjectures issue. AI: no source credits an AI system with any of the generalized-moonshine mathematics. The only AI link is the formal-conjectures issue, whose text says it was 'generated by an AI agent' with no system named; that is authorship of the problem description, not mathematics, so it is recorded but not counted as a system. The name 'Moonshine' in arXiv 2606.10806 is an autonomous conjecture-generating agent working on the Neural Jacobian Conjecture, unrelated to the Monster. The AI search was broad (see search block) and turned up nothing beyond these. The closest I came to a claim of AI in this area is the Epoch-benchmark search, which listed no moonshine problem in any source I could read.
competing_reading: Read as open: Part IV is a 2012 preprint never published in a journal and never independently checked in any source found. Its own text leaves the non-Fricke Borcherds–Kac–Moody condition unproven until the 2017 paper, and the 2017 paper (peer-reviewed) explicitly declines to prove the constant claims in full and says the sharper 24th-root refinement rests on open conjectures. So the full conjecture as Norton stated it (roots of unity or 24th roots, and the constant-function case) is not established by any peer-reviewed source. Wikipedia lists the question open, and a 2026 formal-conjectures issue says only special cases are proven. Read as resolved: the Fricke existence argument plus the non-Fricke completion give existence of the generalized moonshine functions for all Monster elements, the root-of-unity refinement is in a refereed journal, and several citing papers (2017 Duncan–Mertens–Ono; 2022 'Topological modularity') treat it as proven. The bare question asks only whether generalized moonshine exists, not whether the 24th-root sharpening holds, so a reader who takes the bare question as the scope would count it resolved, and one who takes Norton's full 2001 formulation would not.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A journal version of Generalized Moonshine IV, or a written expert verification (referee report, survey section, or Lean formalisation) of the Fricke argument and of the non-Fricke completion in 51 constructions. (2) The text of the 51-constructions Section 0.1 and Section 6 read from the PDF, to confirm whether the constant-function and 24th-root claims are disclaimed by the author. (3) A statement from Carnahan or the Carnahan–Miyamoto paper on whether Norton's statement as quoted by Wikipedia includes the constants. (4) The source the formal-conjectures author used for 'only special cases have been proven'. (5) The source behind Wikipedia's 'open' status, and whether editors have seen the Carnahan series. (6) The full text of Tan 2025 and its publication record, to see whether it cites Carnahan's proof as complete or as needing the non-Fricke part. (7) A readable copy of Carbone's 2026 overview, to see its open-problems list.
